newsitem.title: FRANCE: French stocks open buoyant with big jump.
newsitem.headline: French stocks open buoyant with big jump.

text.p: French shares confidently resumed on Wednesday their bullish trend with an opening surge which took the CAC index up one percent within 10 minutes' trading.

Traders said the market was well supported by Wall Street's gains, dollar strength and rising bond markets. French company sales have also been encouraging analysts to upgrade forecasts, giving the market good fundamental support, said one broker.
The blue-chip CAC-40 index was up 26.24 points or 1.02 percent at 2,608.33 at 0915 GMT while the CAC-40 futures contract was up at 2,615 from 2,591 on Tuesday's close.
Michelin bucked the trend, falling 0.73 percent to 339.4 francs, hit by news of a European Commission inquiry into its sales practices, brokers said.

Axa slipped 0.34 percent to 378.5, on disappointment over the net result of its U.S. Equitable unit. Although operating profit was good, the market was not expecting provisions, and there should have been a warning, said a broker.
BNP, up 4.36 percent at 239.5, topped rising financials, which include Societe Generale, up 2.11 percent at 679 and Suez up 2.9 percent at 270.
Cie Bancaire was also among firm financials, up 3.57 percent at 725. Paribas gains two percent to 398.6.

Financials strengthened on Monday, helped by a sector report, but saw a slight sell-off on Tuesday. But with market talk of merger activity and consolidation, investors are piling into banks and financials.
Among insurers, Gan rose 8.8 percent to 122 and AGF was up 6.6 percent at 201.5.
Lyonnaise des Eaux, up 1.23 percent at 577, reported 1996 sales of 91.1 billion francs.
